title: Animations, Transitions & Responsive Design
description: Bring your interfaces to life with smooth CSS transitions and keyframe animations. Make them work on every screen size with mobile-first media queries, container queries, and the full responsive toolkit.
learningObjectives: Add smooth transitions to interactive elements
Write mobile-first responsive layouts with media queries
Use container queries for truly component-based responsiveness
Apply CSS transforms: translate, rotate, scale

sections.content: The transition property animates changes between CSS states (like hover, focus, active). You define which property to animate, how long it takes, and the easing curve.
🎯 Only animate transform and opacity for 60fps performance. Both are GPU-accelerated and don't trigger layout recalculation.

exercises.question: Why are transform and opacity the preferred properties to animate?
options: They are GPU-accelerated and don't trigger layout recalculation
exercises.correctAnswer: They are GPU-accelerated and don't trigger layout recalculation
hints: Think about what happens on the GPU vs CPU during animation
exercises.explanation: Animating width, height, or margin triggers layout (reflow) and paint on every frame — expensive. transform and opacity are handled entirely on the GPU compositor thread, enabling smooth 60fps animations.

sections.content: While transition animates between two states, @keyframes lets you define a full sequence of intermediate steps. The animation property applies the keyframes with full control over timing, repetition, and direction.
💡 animation-fill-mode: both means the element holds the 'from' state before the animation starts and the 'to' state after it ends. Essential for entrance animations.

exercises.question: What does animation-fill-mode: forwards do?
options: Makes the animation run forward (not reverse)
Keeps the final animation state after it ends
Animates only going forward, not back
Applies the style before the animation starts
exercises.correctAnswer: Keeps the final animation state after it ends
hints: 'Forwards' refers to after the animation ends
exercises.explanation: animation-fill-mode: forwards keeps the element in the final keyframe state after the animation completes. Without it, elements snap back to their original style.

exercises.question: Which transform moves an element 20px to the right without affecting surrounding elements' layout?
exercises.explanation: transform doesn't affect document flow — surrounding elements don't move. margin-left and padding-left do affect layout. left: 20px requires a positioned element.

sections.content: Mobile-first means writing base styles for mobile screens and using min-width media queries to progressively enhance for larger screens. This is better than desktop-first because mobile is the harder constraint.
🎯 Standard breakpoints: sm: 640px, md: 768px, lg: 1024px, xl: 1280px. But always add breakpoints where your content breaks, not at arbitrary device sizes.

exercises.question: In mobile-first CSS, which query correctly targets tablets and above?
hints: min-width means: at least this wide
exercises.explanation: @media (min-width: 768px) applies styles when the viewport is 768px or wider. In mobile-first, base styles target small screens, and min-width queries progressively enhance for larger screens.

sections.content: Media queries respond to the viewport width. Container queries respond to the parent container's size. This enables truly component-based responsive design — a card component that adapts whether it's in a sidebar or a full-width grid.

exercises.question: What is the key difference between media queries and container queries?
options: Container queries respond to parent width; media queries respond to viewport width
Container queries don't work on mobile
Media queries can only target screen size
exercises.correctAnswer: Container queries respond to parent width; media queries respond to viewport width
hints: One looks at the screen, the other at the parent element
exercises.explanation: Media queries apply styles based on the viewport (browser window) size. Container queries apply styles based on the width of the component's containing element — enabling components that intelligently adapt wherever they are placed.

capstoneProject.title: Animated Portfolio Page
capstoneProject.description: Build a fully responsive, animated portfolio page that delights on every device and respects user motion preferences.
requirements: Mobile-first layout with 3 breakpoints (sm, md, lg)
At least 4 keyframe animations (entrance, hover pulse, loading spinner, floating badge)
Smooth transitions on all interactive elements (links, buttons, cards)
A CSS-only card flip using 3D transforms
Container query on project cards (switches layout in sidebar vs main)
Dark mode via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) using CSS variables
Responsive images with aspect-ratio to prevent layout shift
